data.body:
AC verification sweep after the production apply.

AC1 SATISFIED. The spend-cap HCL is on origin/main, landed through Gerrit: 8f7417079ad (Restore Bedrock spend cap Terraform), feca8a211ee (Default Bedrock cap inputs from AWS), 90945a0c1eb (Codify the Cost Anomaly Detection grant).

AC2 SATISFIED. A currency scan over the full history of infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf returns no matches for a dollar-amount pattern. No commit message, README, or HCL comment introduced by that change carries a currency amount.

AC3 SATISFIED. Scheduled drift run 35555452105 planned '8 to add, 3 to change, 0 to destroy'. Zero destroys across all 11 resources. The filed hazard -- a plan that proposed destroying live spend-cap resources -- is gone.

AC4 SATISFIED, by applying rather than removing. aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.reviewbot_webhook_auth_rejections is now live; describe-alarms reports rebar-reviewbot-webhook-auth-rejections in state OK. It no longer appears in the plan.

AC5 -- the aws_instance.gerrit in-place user_data change is owned by 4bfa, which is the ticket that will record the decision. Not this ticket's to make.

AC6 NOT SATISFIED as written (it asks for an empty plan). Post-apply the plan is '8 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy'. Every remaining item belongs to another ticket: 8 x lmn_private_context_denied (794e) and aws_instance.gerrit user_data (4bfa). Nothing spend-cap or alarm related remains.

AC7 NOT SATISFIED. Root cause confirmed and it is broader than this bug: the drift lane is plan-only, running under the read-only rebar-terraform-plan OIDC role, and there is no apply lane anywhere in CI. That is the mechanism by which merged infrastructure accumulates undeployed -- precisely how the two fixes applied in this session sat merged but undeployed.
